Title: Melaka PH, Bersatu in talks to form 'PH Plus' for state election
Article:
MELAKA: State Pakatan Harapan is finalising negotiations with parties that share similar aspirations, including Bersatu, to form a PH Plus collaboration to contest the Melaka election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the negotiations were being conducted based on decisions made at a meeting of the PH Presidential Council.
"The negotiations also include Bersatu, but any form of cooperation will only be announced after the negotiation process has been completed," he told a press conference after attending the launch of Amanah's election machinery in Duyong here today.
Also present were Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, who is also agriculture and food security minister, and Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa.
Meanwhile, Adly, who is also deputy defence minister, said the distribution of seats within PH among PKR, Amanah and DAP had been finalised, including the allocation of eight seats to Amanah.
Among the state seats Amanah is set to contest are Bukit Katil, Durian Tunggal, Telok Mas and Merlimau.
Asked about the possibility of collaborating with Barisan Nasional, Adly said no negotiations had been held with the party so far.

Title: MMA calls for tougher enforcement after repeat illegal clinic discoveries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called for tougher enforcement after the latest discovery of suspected illegal clinics and seizure of unregistered medicines and medical equipment.
"What is particularly worrying is that this comes only months after similar illegal clinics were uncovered earlier this year," MMA president Dr L. Sivanaesan said in a statement.
He said the use of unregistered medicines, injections, antibiotics and medical equipment by unqualified or unregistered individuals posed a serious risk to patients and public health. It said inappropriate use of antibiotics could also contribute to antimicrobial resistance.
Healthcare must be provided by qualified and registered professionals at premises registered with the relevant authorities, using only approved medicines and medical equipment in treating patients, Dr Sivanaesan said.
The association called for tougher, sustained and intelligence-led enforcement, including coordinated inspections of suspected premises and regular follow-up inspections at locations previously found to be operating illegally.
Dr Sivanaesan said enforcement must also follow the supply chain, including how unregistered medicines are brought into the country and those who knowingly facilitate their distribution. It also called for stricter checks at the country's entry points to prevent unregistered medicines from entering Malaysia.
MMA said stronger action was needed not only against those operating illegal clinics, but also against the networks supplying and facilitating the unlawful activities.
Dr Sivanaesan said the government should also address healthcare access challenges faced by undocumented migrants, as fear of coming into contact with enforcement authorities might discourage some from seeking care at registered healthcare facilities, leaving them vulnerable to illegal providers.
MMA urged the public not to compromise their health to save a small amount of money, saying treatment from unqualified individuals or illegal clinics might appear cheaper but could result in serious health and financial consequences.
In June, the Health Ministry said it would step up enforcement against unlicensed healthcare premises, including those offering aesthetic medical services, following a rise in complaints.
The ministry said it had received more than 1,020 complaints about unlicensed medical facilities since 2021, with the number increasing each year.
"The
recurrence raises questions
about whether enforcement is sufficiently sustained to prevent such operations from simply resurfacing elsewhere," Dr Sivanaesan said.

Title: 12,575 still waiting for organ transplants as donor numbers rise
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Health Ministry recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year, up from 89 in 2025, but 12,575 patients remain on the waiting list for new organs as of July.
Deputy director-general of health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said the figures, equivalent to about 1.3 deceased donors per million population, showed that public awareness of organ donation had taken root but remained far from satisfactory.
"Compared to international statistics, countries such as the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Spain and others have higher organ acceptance rates, reaching 20 to 30 per million population," he told reporters after officiating the launch of National Organ Donation Awareness Week (MKPO) 2026 here today.
Speaking on this year's theme, "Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku" (My Heirs, Honour My Pledge), he said MKPO carried the message that a person's wish to donate their organs after death was a humanitarian pledge that deserved to be honoured, with family support and understanding.
Dr Azman said many families were unaware of their loved one's wish to donate, which was among the reasons the number of deceased organ donations remained low and more lives could not be saved.
He said although some 450,000 individuals were registered as organ donors, the number of actual donations remained low as families had the final say on whether donation proceeded after death.
"When the time comes, when a donor falls ill due to an accident, brain death or other causes, they can no longer make the decision. So awareness among family members is crucial to honouring the donor's wishes," he said.
Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year's MKPO following encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.
He said Terengganu recorded seven organ or tissue donation procedures this year, while Pahang and Kelantan each recorded one, their first in a long time.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said the Health Ministry would continue efforts to increase the number of actual organ donors through various measures.
These include setting up the National Transplant Council as a strategic platform to improve coordination of the country's organ donation and transplantation agenda.
He added that the ministry would also step up engagement with institutions across all religions to help the public better understand organ donation, including the fact that it does not contradict religious requirements.
"Sustained explanation of the legal and religious aspects is crucial, as confusion over these matters can be a factor deterring people from coming forward as organ donors," he said.

Title: One-off RM1,000 allowance for Perkeso contributors taking jobs over 100km away
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The government will provide a one-off RM1,000 Mobility Assistance Allowance to Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors who secure new jobs located more than 100km from their homes.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said under the Act the allowance would take effect on Oct 1 through amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017.
Among the changes is an increase in the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 per cent to 50 per cent of the remaining unpaid Job Search Allowance for eligible workers who return to employment early.
"The daily Training Allowance will increase from between RM10 and RM20 to RM30, while the maximum Training Fee covered will rise from RM4,000 to RM7,000.
"This means contributors will receive better support to undergo training, improve their skills and adapt to current job market requirements," Ramanan said at the launch of the three-day Mega iLINDUNGu Festival: Kesuma Bersama Rakyat at Strand Mall here.
Ramanan said under the Act, support and protection provided under the Employment Insurance System (EIS) for each contributor amounted to up to RM25,000.
"However, this is subject to eligibility and the benefits received," he said.

Title: Five students arrested over assault of 14-year-old schoolboy
Article:
KUANTAN: A businesswoman was left distressed after her 14-year-old son was allegedly assaulted by several senior students using a broomstick at a religious secondary school in Rompin last week.
What upset the 40-year-old was the school's alleged failure to look into the matter despite being alerted by her son, prompting her to take matters into her own hands, including lodging a police report and "rescuing" her son from the school.
Siti Rohani Yusof said the incident had left her family traumatised, particularly her son, while the alleged lack of action by the school, including its principal and hostel warden, came as a shock.
The mother of two said the incident occurred on Sept 12, when five senior students called her son and his friend to their hostel room at about midnight before advising them not to leave the school premises without permission.
"Suddenly, they blindfolded my son and began punching him in the stomach, kicking his back, slapping his face and hitting him with a broomstick.
"They assaulted him for more than an hour. They even threatened to injure him with a penknife and a piece of glass," she told reporters at her house in Bukit Rangin here today.
She said her son informed the school management about the incident, but no action was taken.
Upon learning that the senior students were planning another assault, her son called and informed his father using a public phone on Sept 16.
Siti Rohani said when she contacted the hostel warden, she was told there was no need for her to travel to the school as the matter had been settled.
"I decided to immediately go to the school and, upon reaching the hostel, I was shocked to see my son's body and hands covered in bruises.
"The seniors allegedly involved in the incident were moving around freely.
"I lodged a police report on Sept 17 and took my son to hospital for a check-up. When I shared details about the incident with other parents, I was informed that several children had previously been assaulted by the seniors but the incidents were never disclosed by the school," she said.
Siti Rohani said she was upset that the school, despite being aware of the incident involving its students, had allegedly chosen to conceal the matter.
"My son was forced to treat his own injuries... I am fortunate that my son is still alive.
"Concerned about my son's safety, I told him to pack his belongings on Sept 16 and I am in the process of transferring him to another school," she said.
Meanwhile, Rompin deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohamad Zamri Mohamad Zaber said police had arrested five students after two victims lodged separate reports at about 1pm on Sept 17.
He said the suspects, comprising three Form Five and two Form Four students, were questioned to assist investigations under Section 147 of the Penal Code for rioting.
The offence carries a maximum two years' imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
"Both victims sustained injuries believed to have resulted from the assault. All the suspects have been released on police bail," he said.

Title: RM10 per member: Umno sets RM30mil goal to help Najib pay court fine
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno is targeting up to RM30 million for the Tabung Solidariti Najib Razak if all of its estimated 3.8 million members nationwide contribute to the fund.
Umno supreme council member Datuk Razlan Rafii said the target was achievable if each member contributed at least RM10.
"Looking at the amount collected so far, we are positive about the support given to the Tabung Solidariti Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
"After this, contributions will be easier once we obtain the bank's QR code, allowing people to use digital platforms to contribute," he said when contacted today.
Razlan said organisers were optimistic that the target could be reached as soon as possible, with no official closing date set for the fund.
Umno launched the fund to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay a RM50 million fine imposed as a condition of his conditional pardon.
Recalling a similar effort in the past, Razlan said he had previously launched a fund in July 2018 to help pay part of Najib's bail in the case involving alleged misappropriation of SRC International funds.
"Previously, we launched a fund to help with Najib's bail and managed to collect RM500,000 within a short period, thanks to the spirit of party members," he said.
On negative reactions on social media to the latest fund, Razlan claimed the opposition was deliberately generated by certain parties using "cyber armies".
"Many support Najib, but we face challenges when certain parties deliberately campaign to shape public opinion in Malaysia.
"These are all paid bots; it is not a true reflection of Malaysians," he said.
Razlan also urged the public to consider Najib's contributions and services fairly.
"Every leader has their contributions and achievements. The wrongs or mistakes they have made should be balanced against their contributions. That is what is most important," he said.
He also commented on the stance previously taken by some government leaders who had said they were prepared to resign if Najib was granted a pardon.
Razlan said the current situation showed how far the leaders concerned valued their positions over their principles.
"Today, we can see how much they value their positions over their principles," he said.

Title: New MyKad: Dyed hair allowed if not too prominent
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Applicants for the new-generation MyKad are allowed to have dyed hair as long as the colour looks natural and is not too prominent.
National Registration Department Identification Card Division director Muhammad Asraf Sukadi said the requirement also took into account an individual's original hair colour, including those with grey hair or who use henna.
He said the department did not require applicants to have black hair, but the colour should closely resemble their natural hair colour and not be excessive.
"We allow hair colours that are close to the original colour. For example, grey hair or hair coloured using henna, as long as it is not too prominent.
"For example, if someone is of Eurasian descent, we allow it, and there is no problem. But it should not be completely blonde. The colour should be more natural," he said during an interview on a programme with radio station Kool FM.
The clarification followed a picture of a new-generation MyKad belonging to a female singer that went viral on social media, prompting discussion over hair colour and several other requirements for identification card photographs.
Meanwhile, he said claims that applicants must wear a black headscarf when having their photograph taken for the new MyKad were inaccurate.
He said the department required applicants wearing headscarves to use dark colours because the background of the MyKad photograph was white.
"We did not say black. We said dark colours because the background is white.
"If they wear a light-coloured headscarf, we will not be able to see it properly in the photograph," he said
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] DAP leaders arrive for emergency CEC meeting over Najib pardon [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke and other party leaders have arrived at the DAP headquarters here for an emergency central executive committee (CEC) meeting.
The meeting is being held following the latest development involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who was granted a conditional pardon.
Loke arrived at 2.54pm, followed by other leaders, including DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo and Wanita DAP chief Teo Nie Ching.
Also spotted arriving for the meeting were DAP deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh, who sits on the Federal Territories Pardons Board, and DAP deputy chairman Nga Kor Ming, as well as other party leaders.
It was reported yesterday that Najib was granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence on condition that he pays the
RM50 million
fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board, in a statement, had said that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
It also said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had consented to the conditional pardon.

Title: RTS Link: Border security preparations stepped up ahead of January launch
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) is stepping up security readiness and border inspection capabilities ahead of the launch of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link in January next year.
MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods.
He said while technology played an important role in supporting enforcement, it could not be regarded as the sole solution to security threats at the country's entry points.
"Technology helps, but it is not the solution to these threats. A combination of both is essential, while how we utilise technology for enforcement is equally important, including training," he told Bernama recently.
Shuhaily said MCBA would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks.
On the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help curb the smuggling of illicit goods, he said the technology needed to undergo a learning phase, including machine learning, before reaching maturity.
"Before AI can mature, it needs to learn through what is known as machine learning. So, it is still a work in progress," he said.
Meanwhile, Shuhaily said 400 MCBA trainees were undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.
He said the trainees were expected to complete their training by the end of September before being deployed to the RTS Link in October.
"We will conduct dry runs over the remaining two months so that by January, everyone is fully prepared to operate this new facility," he said.
Shuhaily said the personnel would initially work alongside senior officers at the Sultan Iskandar Building to gain experience, particularly in inspecting documents and goods.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC chief says media key to anti-corruption efforts
Article:
KAJANG: The media plays a key role in helping the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) combat corruption by delivering accurate and responsible information to the public, its chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said.
He said the commission could not fight corruption alone and regarded the media as one of its key strategic partners.
"In today's fast-moving digital era, the public not only needs information quickly, but, more importantly, they need information that is authentic, truthful, accurate and responsible.
"I sincerely hope the good relationship between the MACC and the media can continue to be strengthened, particularly in ensuring that corruption-related issues are reported professionally, ethically and with integrity," he said.
Abd Halim was speaking at the MACC Shooting Programme with the Media at Kajang Prison College here today.
Also present were MACC Strategic Communications Division director Hisyam Mohd Yusoff, MACC Intelligence Division senior director Datuk Saiful Ezral Arifin, Media Prima Bhd News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim and New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd chief operating officer Luqman Adrine Ja'afar.
Abd Halim said integrity was fundamental to maintaining public trust in journalism, as every report could affect public perception and the reputation of individuals and organisations.
He said news reports could also influence public confidence in the country's institutions.
The MACC remained committed to ensuring information on its enforcement actions and anti-corruption efforts was properly communicated to the public, he said.
Abd Halim said that the fight against corruption went beyond arrests, prosecutions and punishment.
"It is also about prevention, education, awareness and cultivating integrity as a value in our daily lives.
"In this regard, our media partners have a very important role in conveying that message to the people," he said.
Abd Halim expressed hope that engagement programmes with the media would continue and become part of ongoing efforts to strengthen ties between the commission and journalists.
He said the shooting programme also gave media practitioners an opportunity to experience, albeit on a different scale, the level of precision, discipline, focus, emotional control and accuracy required of MACC officers in carrying out their duties.
"When in the field, MACC officers must remain calm and disciplined and exercise sound judgment.
"The use of firearms is not merely about strength or courage. It requires discipline, self-control, compliance with safety procedures and a high degree of responsibility," he said.
Hafidzul Hilmi Mohd Noor, representing Harian Metro, took third place, while Sinar Harian's Muhammad Afham Ramli took second place in the men's centre-fire category.
Meanwhile, Nur Ayuni Johari from Malaysia Gazette took first place in the women's centre-fire category.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australian man pleads not guilty to Thai suitcase murder
Article:
BANGKOK: An Australian accused of murdering a teenage girl in Thailand and abandoning her body in a suitcase pleaded not guilty in court on Friday, citing self-defence.
Simon Peter Carman, 45, was arrested at a Bangkok airport in June as he prepared to take a flight back to Australia, after the 17-year-old victim's friend had reported her missing.
The young woman's body was found in a suitcase near a railway track in Pattaya, a seaside resort city south of the capital Bangkok.
Police said she died of suffocation.
Carman appeared on Friday at Pattaya Provincial Court, where he denied all charges, citing "self-defence and a mistaken belief about the victim's age", a court statement said. It did not elaborate further.
The Australian is charged with murder, concealing a body and taking a minor aged between 15 and 18 for indecent purposes.
The court denied Carman's bail application after prosecutors opposed his release, saying he posed a flight risk. The next court date was set for October 12.
Police previously said CCTV footage showed him entering a condominium in Pattaya with the girl and leaving that evening carrying a large black suitcase.
The case put the spotlight on Pattaya, which is popular with foreign tourists for its beaches and nightlife, but also has a reputation for sex tourism.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 68,177 people lost jobs between January and Sept 16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 68,177 workers lost their jobs between January and Sept 16 this year, an increase of 15,196 from the same period last year.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said workers in the manufacturing and wholesale and retail sectors were among those most affected.
He said although the figure showed an increase, the labour market remained resilient overall, with the labour force and number of employed people continuing to grow as of July this year.
"As of July, the labour force had increased to 17.37 million, while the number of employed people reached 16.85 million, with the labour force participation rate remaining at 70.9 per cent.
"The unemployment rate remained at three per cent, the same as the previous month, involving about 520,300 unemployed people," he said during the Global Supply Crisis Briefing here today.
Akmal said the situation showed that the country's labour market remained stable overall, although certain sectors continued to face pressure.
He said the government remained vigilant about the development, particularly the increase in job losses in affected sectors.
He said the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) had also implemented job placement initiatives through the Employment Insurance System (EIS) and MYFutureJobs portal to help workers who had lost their jobs return to the labour market.
From January to Sept 11, he said 143,653 workers had secured new jobs through the initiatives.
"The development shows that government intervention is not merely about providing temporary support to affected workers, but also helping them secure new employment and return to work.
"It also reflects that although the labour market remains stable overall, continued attention is needed to address job losses occurring in certain sectors," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Workers to get enhanced EIS benefits, training support from October
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Workers will receive enhanced financial and training support from October, with the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) also expanding employment opportunities and social protection initiatives under a broader effort to strengthen Malaysia's workforce safety net.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said amendments to the Employment Insurance System (EIS) Act, passed by the Dewan Rakyat last December, would improve benefits for contributors who lose their jobs and strengthen the system's governance.
Among the changes is an increase in the Early Re-employment Allowance from 25 per cent to 50 per cent of the remaining unpaid Job Search Allowance for eligible workers who return to employment early.
The daily training allowance will increase from between RM10 and RM20 to RM30, while the maximum training fee covered will rise from RM4,000 to RM7,000.
Eligible contributors who secure employment more than 100km from their homes will also receive a new one-off Mobility Assistance Allowance of RM1,000.
The amendments also strengthen Perkeso's role in providing employment services, including job matching, career counselling and other active labour market programmes.
"People who come here should not leave with just information. We want them to go home with employment opportunities, access to social protection and solutions.
"For those looking for a job or seeking to advance their careers, seize this opportunity. We are bringing employers and job opportunities directly to the people," Ramanan said at the launch of the three-day Festival Mega iLindungu: Kesuma Bersama Rakyat at Strand Mall here.
The festival, which runs until tomorrow, features the Lindung Kerjaya Carnival by MyFutureJobs, with 25 employers offering more than 2,000 vacancies with salaries ranging from RM2,000 to RM12,000.
Job seekers can also obtain resume guidance and job-matching services, while visitors can access free health screenings, contribution checks, benefits advice and registration for Perkeso schemes.
The event also saw gig economy platforms Grab, Foodpanda and Haloje Delivery pledge RM1,514,412.40 in Perkeso contributions, expected to benefit about 500 e-hailing and p-hailing riders.
Ramanan said the initiative was important as gig workers and their families needed protection against unexpected risks.
"Behind every rider and driver, there is a family that depends on their income.
"That is why social protection is not something to be taken lightly. It is a vital safety net when something unexpected happens," he said.
Meanwhile, 400 housewives from the Sungai Buloh parliamentary constituency received RM48,000 under the Lindung Kasih Suri Rumah initiative at the event.
The festival brings together Perkeso and 11 agencies under the Human Resources Ministry, offering visitors access to employment, skills development, social protection and other services in one location.
About 60,000 visitors are expected to attend the three-day event, which runs from 10am to 10pm daily.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prabowo welcomes Malaysia's offer to assist in tackling Indonesia forest fires
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has welcomed Malaysia's offer to assist in tackling forest fires in the country, including through the provision of assets and expertise.
He said the offer involved an aircraft, three helicopters and a firefighting team.
He said this after receiving a courtesy call from Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at the President's residence in Hambalang, Bogor, on Friday.
"This is an environmental problem that affects many parties and although the fires are in Indonesia, their impact is also felt by our neighbours, so they want to help us and we welcome the assistance," he said in a video recording uploaded on the social media accounts of Indonesia's Presidential Secretariat and shared by Zahid on his social media account yesterday.
Prabowo said Indonesia had also received offers of assistance from several other countries, including Japan, to help put out the prolonged forest fires, particularly in Kalimantan.
He said Indonesia was also drawing up comprehensive preventive measures to ensure that the same situation did not recur every few years.
Earlier, Zahid, who is currently on a four-day visit to Jakarta, conveyed the offer to Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka on Wednesday.
Malaysia's offer involves a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and Royal Malaysian Air Force.
Prabowo also stressed the importance of maintaining and strengthening Malaysia-Indonesia relations.
He said the meeting also discussed several other matters, including cooperation in the halal industry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH Presidential Council discussed house arrest, not GE16, says Mat Sabu
Article:
MELAKA: The Pakatan Harapan (PH) Presidential Council meeting yesterday focused on the legal and procedural aspects of implementing house arrest, says Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said house arrest was a new concept in Malaysia and its implementation needed to be carefully studied from legal and operational perspectives.
Mohamad said matters concerning its implementation had been left to the relevant authorities, particularly the Attorney-General, to examine the necessary procedures and standard operating procedures (SOP).
The meeting followed the Pardons Board's decision to grant former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak house arrest for the remainder of his sentence, on condition that he pays the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.

The Pardons Board also said Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
"The general election was not discussed at yesterday's PH Presidential Council meeting. What was discussed was how to handle this new situation regarding house arrest," said Mohamad, who is commonly known as Mat Sabu.
"This is something new in Malaysia. In terms of the law and other aspects, it will be studied," he said after launching the Melaka Amanah election machinery in Duyong.
Asked about the timing of the next general election, Mohamad said the decision rested with the prime minister, although he hoped it would be held towards the end of next year.
"For the prime minister, it can be anytime he deems suitable. It is his right to decide," he said.

Title: Malaysia to study proposal for India's BrahMos missile system
Article:
LUMUT: Malaysia will study a proposal to acquire India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
"Whatever it is, we will study it for each service. If this is for air-to-surface missiles, it comes under the Air Force, so we will study it," he said.
He said the proposal, which was raised during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's recent visit to India, would first be studied by the Royal Malaysian Air Force.
"Whenever not only the prime minister, but ministers as well, travel anywhere, there are many parties wanting to
sell
all kinds of things," he said.
He told reporters this after opening the 93rd Armed Forces Day celebrations at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
He said the assessment would also consider the implications of integrating the proposed missile system with existing equipment, including whether upgrades would be required for the Sukhoi fighter jets.
"We also have to look at our defence doctrine," he said.
Khaled said Malaysia's existing missiles had a range of slightly more than 100km, while the proposed system had a range of between 300km and 400km.
"So, who are we going to fire at? That depends on our defence doctrine," he said.
The BrahMos system is a long-range, ramjet-powered supersonic cruise missile jointly developed by India's Defence Research and Development Organisation and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya through their joint venture, BrahMos Aerospace.
The missile can be deployed from multiple platforms, including land-based mobile launchers, warships, submarines and fighter aircraft, giving operators flexibility in conducting precision strikes against targets at sea and on land.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH will contest Melaka election regardless of cooperation outcome, says Fuziah
Article:
KUANTAN: There has yet to be any decision on potential political cooperation for the Melaka election, but Pakatan Harapan (PH) will contest the polls regardless of the outcome.
PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the coalition was ready to enter the election battleground and face its opponents in the Melaka state election.
"No decision has been made regarding political cooperation for the Melaka state election, but the fight goes on.
"Whatever the outcome, we are prepared to contest in Melaka," she told reporters after opening the Madani Kita programme at Dewan Serbaguna Sungai Isap Damai here today.
She was commenting on talks over possible political cooperation with Barisan Nasional to contest the Melaka election.
On rumours that PH would cooperate with Bersatu in the Melaka election, Fuziah said there had been no official decision or announcement on the matter.
Meanwhile, Fuziah reiterated that PH would continue its fight against corruption and would not tolerate any form of misconduct or abuse involving corrupt practices.
"PH would not accept any situation involving corruption, abuse of power or misappropriation, and would remain committed to ensuring that such wrongdoing is looked into.
"The PH Presidential Council remains firmly behind Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Attorney-General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh,
that no one is above the law
and the Constitution is supreme," she said.
She was commenting on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional house arrest order, which allows him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to a RM50 million fine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brazil police nab suspected serial killer disguised as woman
Article:
RIO DE JANEIRO: Brazilian police said Friday they had captured a suspected serial killer linked to at least 16 deaths since May, who was arrested while disguised as a woman and carrying a baby.
He claims to have killed more than four times that number.
The suspect was arrested Sunday after a 30-hour police manhunt in a forested area of Paraiba state in northeastern Brazil.
He was wearing a dress and long black wig, which police described as a disguise to evade capture. In a statement, they said he had been carrying a baby in his arms.
Local media reported the child was not related to the suspect. Police did not release details on the baby's condition or say where it came from.
"Although the suspect claimed involvement in 80 homicides, civil police have confirmed his participation in 16 killings in the region, 11 of which he confessed to during questioning," police told AFP.
The 16 homicides all took place since May. The identities of the victims and details of the killings have not been made public.
The suspect evaded an earlier attempt to arrest him a few weeks ago after a confrontation with security forces, who consider him a member of an "ultra-violent" criminal group.
In a video of his interrogation obtained by AFP, the man said he acted alone and denied having ties to organised crime.
Instead, he claimed that all his victims were "linked to the criminal world" and that he was taking justice into his own hands in response to threats against himself and his family.
"I never acted against any family man, mother or working person," he said, denying being a "psychopath."
He said he had committed his first homicide at the age of 13.
After the earlier attempt to arrest the suspect, police seized bulletproof vests, the stock of a submachine gun, and over 100 rounds of ammunition, which the man acknowledged were his during questioning.--AFP

Title: Israeli, Lebanese armies face off after Israeli advance in south Lebanon
Article:
DEÏR MIMASS, Lebanon: Israel's military moved forward on Friday in a south Lebanon village, facing off against a Lebanese army position and detonating stun grenades, Lebanon's army and an AFP photographer said.
Israel has been occupying a swathe of south Lebanon since war broke out in March against Lebanese group Hizbollah, but the Lebanese army is supposed to gradually take control of the area under a framework agreement between the two countries.
Under the deal, Iran-backed Hizbollah is meant to disarm and Israel to withdraw from Lebanon, but progress has been slow, with Israel warning it will stay put as long as its foe remains a threat.
In the village of Deir Mimas on Friday, located on the edge of territory occupied by Israel, two Israeli tanks advanced along a road towards the settlement, the AFP photographer saw.
The tanks stopped in front of a barricade made from earth, beyond which Lebanese army vehicles were stationed.
The Lebanese army said in a statement late on Friday that Israeli forces approached an observation post, established on Sept 10 in coordination with the ceasefire monitors, and launched stun grenades "in its vicinity."
In response, the army "reinforced the post, and a state of heightened alert ensued between the two sides", it said.
Lebanon's state-run National News Agency (NNA) had earlier reported a similar version of events, saying the Israelis threw six stun grenades.
According to the AFP photographer, the Lebanese army withdrew by about 100 metres but remained in a position facing the Israeli tanks.
The army said the Israelis later left the area and army personnel returned to their "main position" in the village.
It recently established itself at the site and also has a presence at other locations in Deir Mimas on the edge of the Israeli-occupied zone, according to the photographer.
But the Lebanese army has stayed out of hostilities between Israel and Hizbollah.
The group dragged Lebanon into war with Israel on March 2 in support of its Iranian patrons. Israel responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion of the south.
On Thursday, a meeting was held between Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, French President Emmanuel Macron and Jordan's King Abdullah II to muster international support for Lebanon's army as it seeks to take control of south Lebanon.
Separately, the NNA reported that Israeli forces had set fire to a government hospital in the town of Mays al-Jabal, inside Israel's self-declared security zone.
Lebanon's health ministry condemned it as a "barbaric crime." --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Home Ministry, Prisons Dept await Pardons Board letter on Najib's house arrest
Article:
KULIM: The Home Ministry and Prisons Department have yet to receive an official letter from the Pardons Board on the conditional house
arrest
granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry would wait for formal notification of the board's decision before determining its next course of action.
"At the Home Ministry, which oversees the Prisons Department, we will wait for the official letter informing us of yesterday's decision by the Pardons Board.
"As of now, we have not received anything," he said after visiting the families of four children who drowned in Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan.
"Only after receiving the notification will it be clear what further action we will take, in line with existing legal provisions."
Saifuddin said the ministry would need to examine the contents of the letter to understand the details of the decision, including whether the location for Najib's house arrest had been specified or left to the Prisons Department to determine.
"I need to see the letter first. Currently, Datuk Seri Najib is serving his prison sentence.
"House arrest means he will not be in prison but at another premises, and there are naturally processes to follow," he said.
Saifuddin said the ministry needed clarity on the decision before taking any action to ensure that its implementation complied with the Pardons Board's ruling.
Najib previously had his prison sentence reduced from 12 years to six years and his fine cut from RM210 million to RM50 million.
"If Datuk Seri Najib pays the reduced fine of RM50 million, his release date will be Aug 23, 2028.
"If the fine is not paid, he will be released on Aug 23, 2029," Saifuddin said.
On house arrest more broadly, Saifuddin said Malaysia currently had no specific legislation governing such a mechanism.
However, he said the ministry had obtained cabinet approval in principle to begin drafting a House Arrest Bill for tabling in Parliament.
He said the proposal was originally intended to address prison overcrowding, particularly among remand detainees.
"We currently have 41 prisons housing about 93,000 inmates, despite a total capacity of only 75,000.
"That is why I obtained cabinet approval in principle to begin the process of tabling a House Arrest Act to address prison overcrowding," he said.
Saifuddin said that if the bill were passed, certain remand prisoners could be placed under house arrest, with their movements monitored using electronic devices until their trial dates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MIC's Sivaraj seeks clarity on 30 pct Bumiputera equity rule for tuition centres
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MIC National Strategic Director Datuk C. Sivaraj has called on the Education Ministry to clarify the proposed 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for tuition centres.
"We need to distinguish between helping Bumiputera obtain ownership and taking ownership that has been legally acquired by others," he said in a statement.
The rule would require tuition centres to have at least 30 per cent Bumiputera equity, with implications for existing operators from 2027.
Sivaraj said efforts to increase Bumiputera participation in the economy should not come at the expense of the rights and equity of non-Bumiputera communities through licensing conditions, rulings or administrative regulations.
Existing business owners who have invested their own capital, taken risks and complied with regulations should not be required to give up part of their equity to obtain or renew a licence, he said.
Sivaraj said if failure to secure a Bumiputera partner could result in a licence not being renewed, it raised the question of whether the partnership was truly voluntary or whether the operator had no choice.
He said the Government's power to formulate policies should be exercised carefully, particularly when they involve businesses that have operated legally for many years.
"We cannot empower one race by sacrificing the rights of another," he said.
Sivaraj said if the aim was to increase Bumiputera ownership, more opportunities should be created through financing, training, contracts, market access and new ventures, rather than relying on existing owners to achieve that objective.
He said the policy also affected many Indian operators who had built their education businesses over many years, invested their own money, taken risks, employed workers, paid taxes and served the community.
"The economic rights of the Indian and non-Bumiputera communities cannot be treated as something that can be reduced with every policy change. If we want to build a united Malaysia, the rights and contributions of every community must be respected.
"I support efforts to increase Bumiputera economic participation, but at the same time, I will defend the rights of the Indian and non-Bumiputera communities when their economic interests are affected," Sivaraj said, adding that Bumiputera participation could be increased without confiscating equity from other communities.
Sivaraj urged the Education Ministry to clarify whether the 30 per cent requirement would apply to existing tuition centres, the transition period and what would happen to operators unable to meet it.
"Helping Bumiputera does not necessarily mean taking from non-Bumiputera," he said.
"We can increase Bumiputera participation without taking away the equity of other communities, and build the success of one community without making another community a victim," he said.
The New Straits Times has reached out to the Education Ministry for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump: Son to repay Russian oligarch who funded wedding parties
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Friday his son, Donald Trump Jr., has told him he would pay back a Russian oligarch who bankrolled wedding celebrations for him in the Bahamas in May.
Democrats in the US Congress launched an investigation ‌this week into reports that Umar Kremlev, a wealthy Russian businessman and president of the International Boxing Association, paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for the wedding festivities.
ProPublica, which first reported Kremlev's involvement, said he has close ties to the Russian government.
Trump told reporters on Friday that when he asked his son about the report, he responded, "'No, I'm paying it back, Dad.' And that was a while ago. So I heard he's paying."
A person familiar with the situation confirmed that Don Jr. planned to reimburse Kremlev.
Kremlev and the IBA did not immediately respond to requests for comment late on Friday.
The president, who did not attend his son's wedding, said in a statement earlier in the week that he does not know Kremlev and that ​the wedding controversy is "not a ​big deal!"
Trump said on Friday he has given wedding parties to "numerous people" at "beautiful places" like his Mar-a-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida.
"They get married, I give them a party," Trump said. "With all of that being said, I understand that Don's paid him back."
Don Jr.'s wife, Bettina Trump, in an Instagram post on Monday called Kremlev a friend who ⁠extended an "extraordinarily generous wedding gift," stressing that Kremlev paid for two after-parties, not the wedding itself.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Child assault case: Don't paint all soldiers with same brush, says Khaled
Article:
LUMUT: The assault of a child by a soldier should not be used to portray all members of the armed forces in a negative light.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said such incidents were not confined to military personnel and could also occur among members of the public.
"Assaulting a child is not something that only happens among military personnel. Ordinary people also commit such acts.
"So, we should not exaggerate the matter as though all military personnel are like that," he told reporters after opening the 93rd Armed Forces Day celebrations at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
Khaled said the armed forces would continue to pay attention to such cases and provide the necessary guidance and advice to its personnel.
He said the incident should not be used as a basis for making general accusations against members of the armed forces.
"We have to be careful and work together to ensure that this incident is not used as a basis to accuse all military personnel of behaving in such a manner.
"Other people face similar problems too. Perhaps the individual has his own personal issues," he said.
Khaled said the armed forces would continue to provide guidance, counselling and advice where necessary.
"We regard this as something that needs our attention. We will provide guidance, counselling, advice and other forms of support, as we normally do," he said.
It was reported on Thursday that a 40-year-old soldier was charged at the Kota Baru Sessions Court with abusing his five-year-old daughter by kicking her at an eatery.
Police had earlier tracked down a man and a young girl believed to be his daughter to assist in investigations following a viral video showing the man acting aggressively towards the child and kicking her at an eatery.
The man was later
arrested
after surrendering at the Pengkalan Chepa police station last Sunday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Helicopters battle wildfire threatening Ecuador's capital Quito
Article:
QUITO: Ecuadoran firefighters backed by helicopters on Friday battled a major blaze on a hill overlooking the capital Quito that has led to the evacuation of dozens of people.
Four helicopters were deployed to extinguish the fire on Casitagua hill, where enormous plumes of smoke were rising into the air.
On the ground, around 100 firefighters were fighting to contain two hotspots, Captain Pablo Andino of the Quito Fire Department told AFP.
The area has "a lot of brush and trees, and the wind gusts are causing the fire to spread very quickly," Andino said, noting that firefighters were "at great risk."
It has not rained for over a month in Quito, creating tinder dry conditions that have abetted the outbreak of several fires, eight of which were still active on Friday.
There have been no reports of injuries or damage to homes so far.
Nearly 50 people were evacuated on Thursday from northern Quito as a precautionary measure.
Quito Mayor Pabel Munoz estimated the area consumed by flames on Casitagua at around 100 hectares.
Two military and police training academies are situated at the foot of the hill, along with residential complexes.
To prevent the flames from advancing, residents "dug a trench and threw dirt into it," Marta Gonzalez, a 68-year-old seamstress living in the area, told AFP.
City authorities have recorded nearly 200 wildfires between June and September, destroying about 1,200 hectares of forest in the capital.
In 2024, Quito faced one of the worst forest fires in decades, when a blaze started deliberately injured six people and destroyed homes. --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Government shortlists three missile systems for navy's LCS
Article:
LUMUT: The government has shortlisted three surface-to-surface missile (SSM) systems from three countries for the Royal Malaysian Navy's Littoral Combat Ships (LCS).
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the selection was now at the final stage, with several issues still requiring the government's decision.
"We are at the final stage. There are several issues that need to be decided, and we need to obtain the government's decision," he said.
He told reporters this after opening the 93rd Armed Forces Day celebrations at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
Khaled said three types of SSMs had been shortlisted.
"Three... three types of surface-to-surface missiles," he said when asked about the number of companies shortlisted.
Asked whether the missiles were from three countries, he confirmed: "From three countries."
However, Khaled declined to disclose the countries or missile systems involved.
"There's no need to know," he said when asked to name them.
It was reported that a decision to ban deliveries of the missile system was made known to Malaysia just days before the scheduled delivery of the surface-to-surface missiles for five Royal Malaysian Navy LCS.
The report also said the decision to ban NSM deliveries was conveyed to Khaled during a meeting with Norwegian officials on April 20, the first day of the Defence Services Asia 2026 exhibition.
Following this, Malaysia issued a notice of demand to a Norwegian defence firm over the cancellation of an export licence for a missile system intended for the Navy's LCS, claiming losses exceeding RM1 billion.
Malaysia had already paid €126 million (RM583 million), equivalent to 95 per cent of the contract value, before the cancellation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah fertiliser probe: Mohamad Sabu confirms giving MACC statement
Article:
MELAKA: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu has confirmed that he had his statement recorded by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist in an investigation into alleged irregularities and delays in the supply of fertiliser in Kedah.
Mohamad, who is also Amanah president, said he spent about 30 minutes giving his statement to MACC over its investigation into the delayed distribution of Additional Compound Fertiliser.
"Yes, it is done. I was called to give a statement, so I went to give a statement.
"It was brief. They called me, asked questions, I answered them and left it to them," he told reporters after the launch of the Amanah Melaka election machinery in Duyong here today.
Also present were Amanah deputy president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof; Amanah vice-presidents Datuk Mahfuz Omar and Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad; and Amanah Melaka chairman Adly Zahari.
Mohamad said it was up to MACC to determine whether the commission was satisfied with the statement given.
He declined to elaborate on the contents of his statement, leaving it to MACC to determine any further action or developments.
On the letter of demand (LOD) related to the issue, Mohamad said he had left the matter to his lawyer in relation to legal action against the owner of an account who allegedly made malicious allegations against him on social media.
"The letter (LOD) depends on the circumstances. I leave it to my lawyer," he said.
Earlier today, MACC confirmed that it had recorded statements from Mohamad and the ministry's secretary-general to assist in investigations into the delayed supply of fertiliser in Kedah.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman had said that
statements
from Mohamad and the ministry's secretary-general, Datuk Isham Ishak, were recorded on Sept 15 and 16 respectively.
It was reported that Kedah MACC had launched an investigation following a complaint by the Malaysian Padi Farmers' Brotherhood Association (PeSAWAH) on Aug 26 over delays in the supply of fertiliser appointed by the ministry to meet the needs of the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) area covering about 100,000 hectares.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MYSA defence intelligence application director appointed to lead armed forces cyber force team
Article:
LUMUT: Brigadier-General Datuk Abd Razak Sipit has been appointed head of the armed forces Cyber Force Nucleus Team, marking the first step towards establishing the country's fourth military service by 2030.
Abd Razak is a senior military officer who serves as the Defence Intelligence Application Division director at the Malaysia Space Agency (MYSA).
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin presented Abd Razak with his appointment certificate during the launch of the 14-member team at the 93rd Armed Forces Day celebrations at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
The nucleus team will study and develop the requirements for establishing the Cyber Force, which will complement the existing Army, Navy and Air Force.
Khaled said the new service was necessary as modern warfare had evolved beyond conventional battlefields, with security threats increasingly taking non-traditional and hybrid forms.
"We are taking this opportunity to launch another domain. So far, we have the Land, Maritime and Air domains.
Now, we are announcing that we will establish a new branch, the Cyber Force.
"Warfare today is not like what we have known before. Security threats come in non-traditional and various forms, including hybrid threats. Warfare is no longer solely based on taking up arms.
"More importantly, with today's technological advancements, the strength of an armed forces also depends on the use of technology. This is what is known as Network-Centric Operations, meaning the use of networks," he said.
He said aircraft, ships and other military assets were increasingly integrated through networks, making cyber capabilities crucial to military operations.
"From a military perspective, if you want to cripple, jam or attack all these systems, you can do so.
"Likewise, if you want to ensure that a country's defence and resilience are not at the level expected, you can attack the infrastructure and systems used by the people," he said.
Khaled said this was why building resilience among the public was also becoming an important aspect of national defence.
"Apart from assets and military readiness, there is also the resilience of the people. With this new form of warfare, threats and challenges will target things that can cause disruption among the people.
"As we have seen, various systems that people depend on, such as electricity and computers, can be targeted.
"They can jam traffic lights, plunge the country into darkness, and attack airports, oil facilities and energy infrastructure. All of these can be attacked through cyber means," he said.
Khaled said the Cyber Force was targeted to be fully operational by 2030, with personnel from the three existing services brought together under the new branch.
He said the armed forces would also recruit personnel with expertise in fields including information technology and artificial intelligence.
He added that the Cyber Force headquarters would be based in Kuala Lumpur, while details of its organisational structure would be determined later.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Cloud seeding operation in KL, Putrajaya, Selangor today and tomorrow, says Nadma
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A cloud seeding operation will be conducted today and tomorrow to reduce the impact of haze in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Selangor.
The operation will be conducted by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) and Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
Nadma director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the cloud seeding operation was being conducted following PM2.5 readings in the affected areas exceeding 150 for more than 24 hours, based on readings issued by the Department of Environment (DoE).
"The operation will involve the relevant agencies, with an RMAF C-130 Hercules aircraft serving as the main asset for the cloud seeding operation.
"However, the operation is subject to weather conditions and the presence of suitable clouds for the cloud seeding process," he said.
He added that the operation was among the government's efforts to help reduce the impact of haze and improve air quality in the affected areas.
According to the DoE's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), air quality monitoring stations in Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur and Selangor were among 17 stations that recorded unhealthy API readings as of 1pm today.
Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 111, while Cheras and Batu Muda recorded readings of 139 and 124 respectively. Shah Alam in Selangor recorded an API reading of 154.
Seven of the air quality monitoring stations that recorded unhealthy API readings were in Sarawak. Serian recorded the highest reading at 176, followed by Kuching at 172, Sri Aman at 166, Samarahan at 165, Sibu at 158, Sarikei at 150 and Bintulu at 103.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Google's Gemini AI carried out cyberattacks, guessed passwords
Article:
WASHINGTON: Google's consumer AI model Gemini hacked multiple systems through guessing login credentials, the company told AFP on Friday, the latest case of rogue AI cybersecurity transgressions, which have generated safety concerns.
The hacks, first reported by the Wall Street Journal, took place in May and were discovered by Google in July.
"In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test," Heather Adkins, Google's vice president of security engineering, told AFP in a statement.
"In all three of these instances, the model stopped," Adkins added, without specifying which organisations were breached.
"We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they've now made to their testing processes."
In July, two OpenAI models escaped the closed environment they were meant to stay in, got onto the internet on their own and broke into the internal systems AI platform Hugging Face.
The incident fed worries that AI giants cannot keep their own models under control, as similar episodes have been reported at Anthropic and China's Moonshot AI.
"These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly," Adkins emphasised.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New RM270,000 fishing hall for Tanjung Bidara community
Article:
Amir Mamat
Pix - Amir Mamat
MASJID TANAH: Fishermen in Kampung Pasir Gembur, Tanjung Bidara, will receive a new RM270,000 fishing hall next month, courtesy of Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.
The initiative aims to ensure the safety and welfare of fishermen when setting out to sea and returning home with their catch.
Pasir Gembur Fishermen Association chairman Rusli Othman said the commitment ends a decade-long wait for a modern facility.
He said the new hall will streamline daily operations for 27 local fishermen, from preparing their gear to landing their daily catch.
"Alhamdulillah, to me this is a major success for Datuk Seri Ab Rauf himself. He has proven that he does not just make empty promises, but is committed to delivering what was pledged to our fishing community.
"Moving forward, launching and hauling boats ashore will be much safer without needing to build momentum like a jet ski. Equipment and boat storage will also be far more organised," he said.
Earlier, Rauf, accompanied by Rural Development, Agriculture and Food Security Committee chairman Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, officiated the groundbreaking ceremony for the facility.
During the event, fishermen were also presented with GPS Finder devices to assist in navigation and locating fish stocks.
Rusli said the local fishing community was delighted to receive the devices, noting that such equipment is usually costly but highly sought after for pinpointing large schools of fish.
He expressed gratitude for the Chief Minister's initiative, adding that the technology will make trips safer and boost catches.
Meanwhile, 60-year-old fisherman Mustaffa Che Man said the new hall brings renewed hope to local fishermen, giving them proper comfort for their daily operations.
Another fisherman, Mohd Fazli Baba, 43, said the GPS devices will help prevent fishermen from getting lost at sea during bad weather or low visibility.
"I once got lost and drifted as far as Pantai Puteri and Pulau Besar because I did not have a GPS device to guide me back.
"Having this device will make it much easier to track fish and navigate back to our hall safely," he said.
In September last year, Rauf visited the site to inspect the previous 40-year-old facility, which had fallen into disrepair.
Following the visit, he convened a meeting with fishermen representatives and relevant government agencies to expedite the construction of the new fishing hall.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fourteen of 20 banks now offer reducing balance hire-purchase financing, says Armizan
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — Fourteen of the 20 banking institutions providing hire-purchase financing had begun offering customers the reducing balance method as of Sept 18, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the remaining six banking institutions are expected to complete the transition to the new method by December 31 at the latest, following engagement sessions with the banks.
“In total, there are 429 entities, comprising banking institutions and hire-purchase providers, registered with the Association of Hire Purchase Companies Malaysia (AHPCM),” he told reporters at the closing ceremony of the Consumer Festival (CONFEST) 2026 at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan added that the ministry had set a target for 80 per cent of hire-purchase providers to offer financing in compliance with the Hire-Purchase (Amendment) Act 2026 by the end of this year.
He noted that hire-purchase providers that are not yet fully prepared have been granted a grace period until March 31, 2027, with full compliance required from April 1 next year.
According to Armizan, the amendments to the Act that took effect on June 1 introduced the reducing balance method and effective interest rate, replacing the flat interest rate and “Rule of 78” method.
“Under this method, interest is calculated based on the current loan balance, making early loan settlement more transparent for consumers,” he said.
CONFEST 2026, themed “
Suara Kita: Kuasa Kita
”, is organised by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) from Sept 17 to 20.
The 2026 National Consumer Day celebration aims to raise public awareness of consumer rights, protection and responsibilities.
The programme brings together consumer advocacy groups, government agencies and non-governmental organisations through a range of activities, including consumer-related competitions, a Fun Walk, a Fun Run and booths hosted by KPDN agencies and strategic partners. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia aims to finalise new e-commerce Bill this year, says domestic trade minister
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Sept 19 — The government aims to finalise the drafting of a new e-commerce Bill this year, said Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali.
He said the ministry had approved the policy decision to repeal the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 and replace it with a new, more comprehensive law.
However, he said the process would require coordination between ministries as well as extensive engagement with stakeholders, including e-commerce platforms, service providers and industry players.
“We know that e-commerce is a broad and comprehensive area, so it requires extensive engagement with stakeholders. We need to examine the matter thoroughly, and I hope it can be finalised,” he told reporters after launching the 2026 Consumer Festival (Confest 2026) at Batu Kawan Stadium here today.
Armizan said two committees had also been established to expedite the drafting of the bill, including to facilitate coordination between the ministry, the Ministry of Communications and the Ministry of Digital.
He said matters currently being fine-tuned included the division of responsibilities among the ministries and relevant agencies, as well as the regulatory mechanisms for e-commerce platforms.
The next stage would also require a regulatory impact assessment (RIA) in collaboration with the Malaysia Productivity Corporation (MPC) before the bill is submitted for further consideration.
Among the proposals being studied is the introduction of a licensing regime for e-commerce platforms, particularly in view of the influx of goods from overseas, consumer safety and the sustainability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
However, Armizan said regulation must be balanced so as not to hamper the growth of the e-commerce sector, which provides convenience to consumers and serves as a source of income for traders.
“We want more comprehensive and conducive regulation, but at the same time, we do not want to hamper the growth of e-commerce,” he said.
The government had previously expressed its intention to expedite the drafting of the e-commerce Bill to strengthen the regulation and accountability of platforms, sellers and consumers, given that the Electronic Commerce Act 2006 does not provide a comprehensive legal framework to regulate various aspects of e-commerce. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia records 102 deceased organ donors so far in 2026, but 12,575 still await transplants, says MOH
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 19 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) recorded 102 deceased organ donors from January to August this year.
Deputy Director-General of Health (Medical) Datuk Dr Azman Yacob said this is an increase from the 89 deceased organ donors in 2025, equivalent to roughly 1.3 donors per million population.
He said both figures showed that public awareness of the importance of organ donation had taken root, but was still far from satisfactory, with 12,575 patients still on the waiting list for new organs as of July this year.
“Compared to international statistics, countries such as the UAE (United Arab Emirates), Spain and others have higher organ acceptance rates, reaching 20 to 30 per cent per million population,” he told reporters after officiating the launch of National Organ Donation Awareness Week (MKPO) 2026 here today.
Speaking on this year’s theme, “
Warisku, Hormati Ikrarku
” (My Heirs, Honour My Pledge), he said MKPO carries the message that a person’s wish to donate organs after death is a humanitarian pledge that deserves to be honoured and affirmed through their family’s support and understanding.
Dr Azman said many families are unaware of their loved one’s wish to donate, which is among the reasons deceased organ donation numbers remain low, and why more lives are not being saved.
He noted that although some 450,000 individuals are registered as organ donors, the number of actual donations remains low, since families have the final say on whether donation proceeds after death.
“When the time comes, when a donor falls ill due to an accident, brain death or other causes, they can no longer make the decision. So awareness among family members is crucial to honouring the donor’s wishes,” he said.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said Terengganu was chosen to host this year’s MKPO in light of encouraging progress in organ and tissue donation across the East Coast states, reflecting growing public awareness.
He said Terengganu recorded seven organ or tissue donation procedures this year, while Pahang and Kelantan each recorded one, their first in a long time.
Meanwhile, Dr Azman said the Health Ministry will continue to work on increasing the number of actual organ donors through various measures.
This includes setting up the National Transplant Council as a strategic platform to drive better coordination of the country’s organ donation and transplantation agenda.
He added that MOH will also step up engagement with institutions across all religions, helping the public better understand organ donation, including the fact that it does not contradict religious requirements.
“Sustained explanation of the legal and religious aspects is crucial, as confusion over these matters can be a factor deterring people from coming forward as organ donors,” he said. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia gets Indonesia’s green light to help battle Kalimantan fires behind haze
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 19 — Indonesia has given the green light for Malaysia to assist in tackling forest and land fires in Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze affecting neighbouring countries, including Malaysia.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto gave his approval during their meeting at Istana Hambalang in conjunction with his working visit to Jakarta.
“President Prabowo welcomed the offer, meaning he has given approval for Malaysia to join efforts to address the haze and fires in Kalimantan,” he told a press conference here today. — Bernama

Title: Defence Ministry shortlists three missile systems for LCS, says Khaled
Article:
LUMUT, Sept 19 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) is in the final stage of shortlisting a surface-to-surface missile system from three countries to replace the system for the Royal Malaysian Navy Littoral Combat Ships (LCS).
Without disclosing the three countries, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said several issues needed to be finalised before a government decision could be made.
“We are at the final stage. We have shortlisted three surface-to-surface missiles from three countries,” he said at a press conference after officiating the launch of the Cyber Force Nucleus Team in conjunction with the 93rd Malaysian Armed Forces Day at the Royal Malaysian Navy Base here today.
In July, Malaysia decided to immediately halt any procurement of new defence equipment or assets from Norway following the country’s decision to revoke the export licence for the LCS missile system.
Meanwhile, commenting on the possibility of Malaysia acquiring the BrahMos air-to-surface missile system from India, he said the matter would be referred to the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) for study.
“If there is a proposal, we will refer it to the RMAF for study, including the implications and integration of the system, as well as upgrading the systems on RMAF defence assets, including the Sukhoi fighter aircraft.
“We will also look at our defence doctrine, because what we currently have has a range of no more than 100 kilometres, while that system has a range of 300 to 400 kilometres,” he said.
Last week, during his visit to New Delhi, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Malaysia was exploring and studying preliminary discussions on acquiring the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system from India. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution says Home Ministry awaits Pardons Board letter, no Najib house arrest notification yet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 19 — The Home Ministry is still waiting for the official written notification of the Pardons Board’s reported decision to place former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak under house arrest before deciding on its next course of action.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry and Prisons Department had yet to receive the letter from the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department, which serves as the secretariat to the Pardons Board.
“Once we receive the notification, only then will we be clear about what further action we need to take, and the steps towards implementing the decision in accordance with the existing provisions of the law.
“As of now, we have not received anything,” he told reporters in Kulim, Kedah today.
He was visiting the families of four young boys who drowned in Taman Desa Kayangan, Sungai Karangan after trying to retrieve a ball.
Saifuddin said the letter would also clarify whether the Pardons Board had specified the premises where Najib would serve his reported house arrest, or whether the matter had been left to the Prisons Department.
“I need to see the letter first. Currently, Datuk Seri Najib is serving his prison sentence. House arrest means he will not be in prison but at another premises, and there are naturally processes to follow. That is why I said I want to see the letter first,” he said.
He said the ministry would also examine whether the Pardons Board’s decision contained any further instructions or delegated authority to the Prisons Department.
“Based on that letter, we will see whether it is limited to the decision of the Pardons Board, or whether the Board has also given further authority to the Prisons Department. We will examine all of that,” he said.
Saifuddin said Najib was currently still serving his prison sentence, adding that house arrest would mean he was no longer held in prison but instead serve his sentence at another premises, subject to the relevant procedures.
He also referred to the Pardons Board’s previous decision to reduce Najib’s 12-year prison sentence to six years and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
Saifuddin said the ministry had subsequently informed Najib that if he paid the reduced RM50 million fine, his release date would be August 23, 2028, while failure to pay would result in a release date of August 23, 2029.
Saifuddin said Malaysia currently had no specific law governing the mechanism for house arrest.
He said he had previously obtained Cabinet agreement in principle to begin the process of introducing a House Arrest Act, but the proposal was initially intended to address prison overcrowding, particularly involving remand prisoners.
Saifuddin said Malaysia currently had 41 prisons housing about 93,000 inmates, against a total capacity of around 75,000.
Under the proposed mechanism, remand prisoners could potentially be placed under house arrest and monitored through modern electronic devices until their trial dates.

Title: AKPS steps up border security readiness ahead Johor Bahru‑Singapore RTS Link launch in January
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 19 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) is stepping up its security readiness and border inspection capabilities ahead of the launch of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link in January next year.
AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said preparations were being intensified through the use of technology, personnel training and operational simulations to ensure effective inspection of documents and goods.
He said that despite the important role of technology in supporting enforcement, it could not be regarded as the sole solution to security threats at the country’s entry points.
“Technology helps, but it is not the solution to these threats. A combination of both is essential, while how we utilise technology for enforcement is equally important, including training,” he told Bernama recently.
Mohd Shuhaily said AKPS would also advise operators on suitable technologies to enhance security and mitigate potential risks.
On the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help curb the smuggling of illicit goods, he said the technology needs to undergo a learning phase, including machine learning, before reaching maturity.
“Before AI can mature, it needs to learn through what is known as machine learning. So, it is still a work in progress,” he said.
Meanwhile, Mohd Shuhaily said 400 AKPS trainees were currently undergoing a three-month training programme at the Segamat Police Training Centre ahead of their deployment to the RTS Link.
He said the trainees were expected to complete their training by the end of September before being deployed to the RTS Link in October.
“We will conduct dry runs over the remaining two months so that by January, everyone is fully prepared to operate this new facility,” he said.
Mohd Shuhaily said the personnel would initially work alongside senior officers at the Sultan Iskandar Building to gain experience, particularly in inspecting documents and goods. — Bernama

Title: Preliminary report on Sarawak Flying Doctor helicopter crash due within 30 days, says deputy transport minister
Article:
MIRI, Sept 19 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (BSKU) will issue a preliminary report on the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash on September 8 within 30 days of the accident, in accordance with Annex 13 of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) on Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation.
Deputy Minister for Transport Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the preliminary report would subsequently be presented to the Cabinet, in line with the Cabinet’s decision on September 9.
